1.explanation:
The bug concerns how Nav items are rendered in iconOnly mode, specifically when an item lacks an icon prop. The files most relevant to this logic are: 
- src/nav/nav.jsx: This is the main entry for the Nav component and controls overall behaviors, like the iconOnly prop and rendering logic for children.
- src/nav/item.jsx: This defines the single item rendering, and will need a check for the iconOnly mode without an icon set (so it can render nothing or not be displayed at all).
- src/nav/popup-item.jsx: PopupItem is used for submenus and may also be affected if rendered without icons in iconOnly mode.
- src/nav/sub-nav.jsx: SubNav (submenu) may include logic for iconOnly mode child rendering and must also be checked for the same issue regarding its label and visual representation in iconOnly mode.
These files together encapsulate the rendering logic for the Nav children and their appearances in iconOnly mode, which is where the bug lies.
1.bug_scenario: When the Nav component is set to iconOnly mode but some Nav items do not have an icon configured, the affected items render as empty blanks, causing layout/UX issues (see the image: an item has no icon, but space is reserved for it and nothing renders). This is inconsistent and confusing in the iconOnly context — the expectation is that only items with icons appear, or at least that items with no icon should not render as empty blocks.

2.explanation: These files implement the Nav component and its children (Nav.Item, Nav.Group, Nav.PopupItem, Nav.SubNav). The bug appears when 'iconOnly' mode is enabled but the icon prop is missing, so these components are responsible for rendering the correct markup and should contain the logic that detects whether to display a slot for an icon or not. The fix needs to ensure that in iconOnly mode, items without icons do not render empty/blank space or placeholders. Main entry point 'src/nav/index.jsx' just re-exports these components and doesn't contain the logic. The major logic and rendering is inside the jsx files for nav, item, group, popup-item, and sub-nav, as indicated by both usage patterns and naming conventions for atomic navigation elements.
2.bug_scenario: When the Nav component is set to iconOnly mode and a Nav.Item, Nav.PopupItem, Nav.Group, or Nav.SubNav does not have an icon configured, an empty blank space appears in the navigation bar (as shown in the screenshot and the bug report). This results in a visually broken or confusing UI experience, since rows with missing icons show up as empty slots instead of being omitted or rendered differently in iconOnly mode.
